scope: Real Node SQLite/Zstd/filesystem/process restart with synthetic fixtures; no model or sandbox claim.

results.name: real SQLite, three independent domain chains and global pagination
synchronous cross-table transaction, rollback, UNIQUE and business errors do not fault
agent and session SQL filters apply before LIMIT and preserve global cursor pages
flush covers its captured target after an empty or older shared flush
required fields, malformed refs, oversized envelopes and query budgets reject without fault
outbox high water rejects new records, then drains without unbounded queues
second writer and live lock recovery are blocked; real owner death is explicit
process crash after file fsync and before receipt reexports no duplicate
unacknowledged crash tail is preserved then repaired from durable outbox
actual export I/O failure freezes writes and preserves outbox until explicit recovery
acknowledged truncation is never silently discarded or rebuilt as success
actual artifact publication I/O failure retains bytes and freezes both record and object admission
database hash tampering throws, freezes writes and does not fake repair
32 MiB randomized artifact roundtrip streams with real backpressure and two hashes
cancelled, over-budget and invalid-chunk objects remain incomplete; secret is rejected
early artifact iterator return is not verification; full corrupted stream fails closed
concurrent artifact admission is bounded and rejects a third stream without queueing
abort races a permanently pending source.next without retaining Store writers or accepting late bytes
concurrent close calls share the real drain and lock-release promise
sealed segments are compressed, chained and verified; stored bit flip is detected
process-killed partial artifact remains retained without a complete object reference

limits: Windows directory fsync is unavailable through this portable Node path; file fsync and process crash recovery are exercised.
Store is a trusted local library. Public DatabaseSync is not exposed to an Agent and cannot enforce OS isolation.
